The Name Left Off the Scoreboard

记分牌上漏掉的名字 · 646 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A junior sports federation opened its annual competition on Saturday. The program put cycling first, then an athletic relay and a volleyball final. A professional soccer club hosted an indoor event beside the track. Ali had earned qualification in the relay after placing third twice. The printed ranking still called him an alternate. A coach asked him to wait beside the oval. He had trained for endurance through winter. One number from the wrong round could keep him out of a championship.

2The referee requested the entry list. A clerk had copied the fifth name from cycling instead of the fifth from athletics. The rider was preparing for a separate medal event, not for a relay. A veteran trainer suggested a different heat. Ali asked if the organizer could use a consistent rule. In bowling or skating, moving a contestant might be easy. Here a later start would make his time harder to compare. The starter held the group until the clerk checked.

3A professional rival wanted the race to begin. A delay could disrupt hockey, badminton, and rugby fixtures. Another athlete thought an amateur should not get a special chance. The coach showed the result from successive trials. Its qualification standard covered every competitor regardless of league. A sportsman who hoped for promotion would be hurt by a wrong list as much as a child from a small club. The organizer postponed the opener and corrected the list.

4While they waited, Ali helped an athlete in a wheelchair get past a stack of hockey equipment. The athlete was competing in a separate race and wanted to know where the first turn began. A rough patch near the outside lane could slow one wheel. They asked the referee to move a loose mat before the opening lap. The rival who had objected came over to help. He had trained on the oval for years and could point to the safest route around the bend.

5The relay began at a quick pace. Ali caught his teammate and made a clean turn. A rival stumbled near the inner line. Ali kept his own lane. His team was beaten by a narrow margin. They felt disappointment, yet nobody called another runner a loser. The referee confirmed the result and Ali congratulated the champions. He had pursued a place in the race. He could respect the finish once he had received that place.

6While results were checked, an official described the next events. A boxing club used the indoor hall and a marathon group shared the road outside. A foot injury made its favorite runner quit the tour. A fellow athlete had been selected in his place. The official gave both names to the announcer. Their example showed why the correct division mattered long before a race ended or an Olympic champion won a medal.

7At the award ceremony a clerk read the team members aloud. Ali's name was still missing on the screen. The organizer stopped and corrected the display before anyone received a gold medal or trophy. A young sportswoman asked why the club had paused twice for one name. The referee pointed to the record and explained that both corrections came from the same mistake. She could see the difference between earning a place and having it properly recorded. The second correction made the first one visible to the audience.

8Ali taped the scoreboard above his bag. A courier brought the revised list to the next venue, where the eighth and ninth names belonged to a different event. The clerk asked if the delay had upset him. Ali said rivalry made every correction feel personal at first. An athlete could be lucky enough to win a medal or narrowly lose it. Both should have a chance to check their place before elimination began. He was confident enough to show the next starter how to read the list.

四级汇总词汇 · 30中文译文

记分牌上漏掉的名字

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1周六，青少年体育联合会开办年度赛事。赛程先是自行车，再是田径接力和排球决赛。职业足球俱乐部也在跑道旁办室内项目。阿里两次跑第三，获得接力资格，印好的排名却还把他列为替补。教练请他在椭圆跑道旁等着。他练了整冬的耐力，一个抄错轮次的名次却可能让他进不了锦标赛。

2裁判要了参赛名单。文员抄了自行车的第五名，没有抄田径的第五名。那个骑手在备另一项奖牌赛，不该出现在接力跑道。老教练提议让阿里去另一组。阿里问能不能按统一规则来。保龄球或滑冰也许容易挪一个参赛者，这里的起跑时间一换，成绩就不好比了。发令员让队伍先等文员核对。

3职业俱乐部的对手想赶紧开跑，怕耽误曲棍球、羽毛球和橄榄球的赛程。另一人觉得业余队员不该得到额外机会。教练拿出连续几次试赛的结果。资格标准对不同联赛的参赛者都一样。错名单既会影响想升级的运动员，也会影响小俱乐部的孩子。组织者推迟开跑，把名单改过来。

4等待时，阿里帮一位坐轮椅的运动员绕过一堆曲棍球器材。那名运动员参加另一场比赛，想知道第一个弯在哪儿。外道的粗糙地面会拖住一只轮子。他们请裁判在开跑前移走松垫。原先反对等待的对手也来帮忙。他在这条跑道上练了很多年，知道怎样过弯最稳。

5接力开始就很快。阿里赶上队友，利落转弯。对手在内线附近绊了一下，阿里守住自己的道。最后他那队以很小的差距败了。大家失望，却没把另一个跑手叫作失败者。裁判确认结果后，阿里向冠军道贺。他争取到的是一次参赛机会。上了跑道，他也能接受终点的结果。

6核对成绩时，工作人员介绍后面的活动。拳击社用室内馆，马拉松队共用外面的路。最受欢迎的跑者脚伤退出巡回赛，另一名队友替上。工作人员把两个名字都交给播报员。这让人明白，早在比赛结束或奥运冠军领牌前，分组和名单就已经很重要。

7颁奖时，文员当众读队员名单。屏幕上还是缺阿里。组织者在颁出金牌或奖杯前暂停，改了显示。一位年轻女运动员问，为什么为了一个名字停了两次。裁判指着原记录说，两次都是纠正同一个错误。挣得参赛名额是一回事，名额正确写进记录又是另一回事。第二次更正让观众也看见了第一次为何需要。

8阿里把记分牌的副本贴在训练包上。一位信使把改过的名单送到下一个赛点，那里第八、第九个名字属于另一项比赛。文员问阿里有没有为耽误不快。阿里说，竞争紧张时，每次更正都会让人觉得针对自己。运动员可能幸运得牌，也可能只差一点。淘汰开始前，两人都该能核对自己的位置。他有把握教下一个参赛者怎么看名单。
